title: The Importance of Attention . . . Is Importance
coreMove: Notice when attention is silently upgrading one factor from present to important.
sourcePressure: The source says attended items gain extra perceived importance at decision time, sitting between privileged moments and focal-as-causal logic.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The most noticeable factor is naturally the most important factor.

hook: An abstract claim that attention changes everything
A generic meeting where someone makes a better pitch
A clever sentence about persuasion before any concrete object appears
counterintuition: You think persuasion happens during the ask, but it happens before it
The obvious factor is not always the important one
Influence is not manipulation when used well
tryThisNow: Set a timer and reflect on attention
Write down three ways to be more persuasive
Ask yourself what matters most right now

exampleSpecs.audience: a chef deciding which fix gets budget before inspection
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a vivid broken tile steals weight from a quieter refrigeration risk
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the chef covers the cracked tile photo and watches the team finally notice the temperature log failures
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a clipboard of cooler readings under a red grease-pencil line

exampleSpecs.audience: a bank designer choosing what customers see first
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a flashy fee waiver makes the due date feel less important
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the designer swaps the hero badge for the actual deadline and watches test users change what they remember
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a mobile mockup with a large due date at the top

exampleSpecs.audience: a nurse checking which symptom parents report as most serious
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a rash photo crowds out breathing details
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the nurse turns the tablet face down and asks for the last difficult breath before discussing the rash
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a parent scrolling to a bright rash photo in the exam room

exampleSpecs.audience: a buyer deciding whether to purchase a van
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether shiny paint overweights the ignored maintenance record
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the buyer makes the seller read the service gap aloud before stepping back to admire the repaint
exampleSpecs.firstImage: sunlight flashing on a newly painted cargo door

exampleSpecs.audience: an organizer allocating guards after a loud complaint
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether one angry vendor outweighs a quiet bottleneck at the west gate
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the organizer pins foot-traffic counts over the complaint email before assigning the guards
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a site map taped to a folding barricade

exampleSpecs.audience: a panel judging applicants with uneven essays
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a polished opening paragraph makes need feel smaller
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the chair has reviewers read the financial-aid line first, then return to the essay
exampleSpecs.firstImage: three application packets clipped with colored tabs

skillTargets: repair decisions distorted by a loud but minor cue
explain why unattended factors get underweighted

tryThisNowSpec: Look at one decision in front of you and circle the factor getting the most attention, then name one quieter factor that deserves weight before you choose.
